hero.headline: St. Petersburg Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: Use St. Petersburg's waterfront, museums, murals, gardens, and Tampa Bay access as the spine of the guide.

overview: Use St. Petersburg's waterfront, museums, murals, gardens, and Tampa Bay access as the spine of the guide.
Keep St. Pete Beach, Clearwater, and other Gulf communities correctly separated from the City of St. Petersburg.

highlights.title: St. Petersburg essentials
highlights.description: Use the destination's defining landscapes, neighborhoods, and cultural sites to structure the visit.

highlights.title: Outdoor access
highlights.description: Build in time for the water, parks, preserves, or trails that genuinely define St. Petersburg.

highlights.title: Local context
highlights.description: Keep nearby municipalities and protected lands distinct so the itinerary stays geographically accurate.

highlights.title: Practical pacing
highlights.description: Group stops by area and leave room for weather, traffic, and seasonal conditions.

thingsToDo.title: St. Pete Pier and bayfront parks
thingsToDo.description: Walk the pier and linked waterfront parks for Tampa Bay views and an easy orientation to downtown.

thingsToDo.title: The Dalí Museum
thingsToDo.description: Visit the major Salvador Dalí collection and distinctive waterfront building as one of the city's signature cultural stops.

thingsToDo.title: Central Avenue and murals
thingsToDo.description: Move west from downtown along Central Avenue for murals, independent shops, breweries, galleries, and neighborhood dining.

thingsToDo.title: Sunken Gardens
thingsToDo.description: Use this long-running botanical attraction for dense tropical plantings and a shaded break from the urban core.

thingsToDo.title: Downtown museum district
thingsToDo.description: Pair the Museum of Fine Arts and other central museums with the waterfront during hot or rainy afternoons.

thingsToDo.title: Gulf beaches — separate municipalities
thingsToDo.description: Plan St. Pete Beach and other Gulf communities as a separate beach day across the peninsula rather than calling them city neighborhoods.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Cooler months are easiest for outdoor planning
bullets: Late fall through early spring generally brings lower humidity and comfortable outdoor conditions.
Summer is hot, humid, and storm-prone; start exposed activities early and keep afternoon plans flexible.
Busy winter and holiday periods reward advance reservations for popular tours and timed attractions.

travelTips: Group each day by geography instead of crossing the region repeatedly.
Use early mornings for exposed outdoor activities and waterfront time.
Check park, marine, and weather conditions before nature-focused plans.
Treat nearby municipalities and protected areas as separate destinations with their own access rules.

faq.q: How many days should I plan for St. Petersburg?
faq.a: Two to three days is a good starting point for the core sights plus one outdoor or regional experience.

faq.q: Is St. Petersburg good for outdoor travelers?
faq.a: Yes. The strongest itineraries combine the destination itself with nearby water, parks, preserves, or trails.
It depends on the destination, but a car or guided tour is often useful for protected lands and regional excursions.

faq.q: Should I book tours in advance?
faq.a: For high-demand wildlife, boating, park, and holiday-period experiences, advance booking is sensible.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: St. Petersburg is an incorporated city on Tampa Bay known for waterfront parks, museums, murals, dining, and outdoor access.

sections.heading: Geography & setting
paragraphs: The city occupies the Pinellas peninsula between Tampa Bay and the Gulf; the Gulf beach towns are separate municipalities.

sections.heading: History & culture
paragraphs: Downtown, the Edge District, Grand Central, and Central Avenue form a strong arts-and-food corridor.

sections.heading: Outdoor & seasonal highlights
paragraphs: Bayfront parks, cycling, boating, and nearby county or state-managed coastal lands complement the museum scene.

sections.heading: Getting around
paragraphs: Downtown is compact; use a separate travel block for Gulf beaches, Fort De Soto, or Clearwater.
